title: Equilibrium Rainbow Display
description: Investigate six reversible chemical systems one tray at a time, prepare source-faithful stocks, predict and apply teacher-approved stresses, record equilibrium evidence and uncertainty, and design an evidence-backed six-color display.
audience: Advanced high-school chemistry learners studying dynamic equilibrium, equilibrium expressions, and Le Châtelier responses.
learningGoals: Predict and explain qualitative equilibrium shifts caused by concentration, removal, temperature, and pressure-volume changes.
Prepare the six source-stated stock systems with correct stated quantities, sequence, safety constraints, and approximation language.
Distinguish observation from explanation and use color only as qualitative evidence for relative species changes.
Design and defend a six-color display that uses red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet while maximizing distinct approved stress types.
safetyNotes: Splash-proof goggles are mandatory; glove use is optional in the source procedure.
Some solutions can cause skin burns and eye damage. Wash skin contact with copious water.
Turn off all flames before handling 95% ethanol.
Concentrated ammonia and 12 M HCl require teacher approval and small, dropwise additions while stirring.
Direct the syringe away from people and toward a wall or floor before changing pressure.
Only instructor-configured disposal procedures are represented; no drain-disposal rule is assumed.
